title: Ladder 1 · Latin only (× 3)
summary: Latin only. Rebuilt 24 Oct: the top of every ladder now comes back at least 3 times (if…, that…, comparisons, questions), every new word is used 3+ times, and it is about 50% longer. Latin read from IPA (v as v), free voices.
pairs: I want to go to work.
I will go to work tomorrow.
Tomorrow I will not go to work, but I will work at home.
Crās ad labōrem nōn ībō, sed domī labōrābō.
I will work at home, that is, with my family.
Domī labōrābō, id est cum familiā meā.
Why do you work at home? Because I see my son.
Cūr domī labōrās? Quia fīlium meum videō.
My wife thinks that I work better at home.
Uxor mea putat mē domī melius labōrāre.
What do you like to play?
I like to play with a ball.
I will see my son this evening.
This evening I will see my son, and we will play outside with a ball.
Hodiē vesperī fīlium meum vidēbō, et forīs pilā lūdēmus.
If it is raining, we do not play outside.
I know that my son likes to play outside.
Sciō fīliō meō placēre forīs lūdere.
Who plays better with a ball? My son, not I.
Quis melius pilā lūdit? Fīlius meus, nōn ego.
I want to see my family.
I have two daughters and a son.
Duās fīliās et ūnum fīlium habeō.
I want to talk with you.
This evening I will talk with my wife and my two daughters.
Hodiē vesperī cum uxōre meā et duābus fīliābus meīs loquar.
How many daughters do you have? Two daughters and one son.
Quot fīliās habēs? Duās fīliās et ūnum fīlium.
If I talk with my daughters, I talk slowly.
Sī cum fīliābus meīs loquor, lentē loquor.
My wife says that I talk too much.
Uxor mea dīcit mē nimium loquī.
How do you say it in Latin?
I am learning Latin because I want to speak Latin.
Linguam Latīnam discō, quia Latīnē loquī volō.
If you speak slowly, I can understand.
Today I understood more than yesterday.
How do you learn Latin? I read stories.
Quōmodo linguam Latīnam discis? Fābulās legō.
If you speak slowly, I understand more.
Because I am tired, I drink too much coffee.
Quia fessus sum, nimium caffeae bibō.
Why do you drink too much coffee? Because I am tired.
Cūr nimium caffeae bibis? Quia fessus sum.
If I am hungry, I eat bread.
My wife thinks that water is better than coffee.
Uxor mea putat aquam meliōrem esse quam caffeam.
This evening I will come home with my son.
Hodiē vesperī cum fīliō meō domum veniam.
If I come home late, my wife is sleeping.
Sī domum sērō veniō, uxor mea dormit.
My wife knows that I am coming home this evening.
Uxor mea scit mē hodiē vesperī domum venīre.
Who is coming with you? My son.
I will get up at six tomorrow.
My son doesn't want to sleep.
Today I got up late, because my son did not sleep well.
Hodiē sērō surrēxī, quia fīlius meus nōn bene dormīvit.
How did you sleep? Not well.
If I get up at six, I am tired.
Sī hōrā sextā surgō, fessus sum.
How many hours did you sleep? Less than my son.
Quot hōrās dormīvistī? Minus quam fīlius meus.
This evening my wife and I made dinner together.
Hodiē vesperī uxor mea et ego ūnā cēnam parāvimus.
If we make dinner together, dinner is better.
Sī ūnā cēnam parāmus, cēna melior est.
My daughters are hungry, that is, they want dinner.
Fīliae meae ēsuriunt, id est cēnam volunt.
When will we have dinner? This evening.
I read a story to my daughters.
Tomorrow I will write my daughters another story in Latin.
Crās fīliābus meīs aliam fābulam Latīnē scrībam.
How many stories have you written? One; tomorrow I will write another.
Quot fābulās scrīpsistī? Ūnam; crās aliam scrībam.
If I write a story in Latin, my daughters don't understand.
Sī fābulam Latīnē scrībō, fīliae meae nōn intellegunt.
Why do you write stories? Because my daughters like them.
Cūr fābulās scrībis? Quia fīliābus meīs placent.
I give my son a ball.
My son gave me the ball, and we played together.
Fīlius meus pilam mihi dedit, et ūnā lūsimus.
Who gave you the ball? My son.
Quis tibi pilam dedit? Fīlius meus.
Give me the ball again, please!
If he gives me the ball, we play again.
Sī mihi pilam dat, iterum lūdimus.
Yesterday I bought bread and milk, but the milk was too expensive.
Herī pānem et lac ēmī, sed lac nimis cārum erat.
How much does milk cost? It's too expensive.
Quantī lac cōnstat? Nimis cārum est.
I think that milk is more expensive than bread.
Putō lac cārius esse quam pānem.
Today I have to work at home, and I need coffee.
Hodiē domī labōrāre dēbeō, et caffeā mihi opus est.
My wife knows that I have to work today.
Uxor mea scit mē hodiē labōrāre dēbēre.
I need coffee, that is, I am tired.
Caffeā mihi opus est, id est fessus sum.
When will you work less? Tomorrow.
Today it is cold, but the sun is shining; let's go outside and walk.
Hodiē frīgus est, sed sōl lūcet; forās eāmus et ambulēmus.
If it is raining, we do not walk outside.
Yesterday it was less cold than today.
Herī minus frīgus erat quam hodiē.
